description: Focused European temporal backfill pass for remaining Dutch and German barracks/training-area rows. Candidate overrides are limited to rows with public source-backed start/end years.

candidate_overrides.name: Boreelkazerne
candidate_overrides.source_notes: Deventer planning/history sources state the Boreelkazerne was built in 1849 and that the site remained military terrain until 1997, when the last military users left and the municipality took control.

candidate_overrides.name: Generaal Majoor de Ruyter van Steveninck Kazerne
candidate_overrides.source_notes: Dutch Defence identifies the kazerne as the current home of the regiment; regimental material documents original 1946 buildings at the Oirschot kazerne. Use 1946 as a conservative facility start floor.

candidate_overrides.name: Koning Willem III Kazerne
candidate_overrides.source_notes: Apeldoorn history page states the Koning Willem III Kazerne was officially taken into use on 10 May 1939. Rijksvastgoedbedrijf confirms current continuing military real-estate use through recent building work.

candidate_overrides.name: Oranje-Nassau Kazerne
candidate_overrides.source_notes: Official site timeline states the kazerne was completed in 1813 and taken into use by King Willem I in 1814; it was transferred to Amsterdam in 1989 and converted to housing/offices.

candidate_overrides.name: Mainfranken-Kaserne
candidate_overrides.source_notes: Local and site brochure sources state the Mainfranken-Kaserne was newly built/opened in 1986 and remains a Bundeswehr location.

candidate_overrides.name: Saaleck-Kaserne
candidate_overrides.source_notes: Engineering project page for the Hammelburg Bundeswehr site states the Saaleck-Kaserne has been used militarily since 1895 and documents current Bundeswehr development work.

candidate_overrides.name: Lager Schwarzenborn
candidate_overrides.source_notes: Hessian historical gazetteer states Lager Schwarzenborn has existed as a military training area since 1936, was a lung sanatorium in 1948-1959, then again a military training area; local history states the Bundeswehr took over/use resumed in 1956.
